- The blurred bars from #132344 flash and distract during replay playback.
- They flash black on player rebuilds and fade in from black on load.

- The first sample paints at once, with no fade from black.

issue.title: fix(recording-api): refuse the dev signing keys on deployed environments
issue.body:
## Problem

- With DEBUG set, a deployed recording-api accepts signing keys that are public in this repo, so anyone could forge block tokens for the public replay block route.
- Block responses carry user-influenced bytes on an app origin without `nosniff`.

## Changes

- A deployed recording-api (`CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT` US, EU or DEV) refuses to start with a dev signing key, even with DEBUG set.
- Local and E2E containers run the production image with the dev keys, so they still start.
- Block responses send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
- Split from PostHog/posthog#132849, which carries the Django and player half.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran the recording-api `auth` and route suites locally.

**Test rationale:** new cases cover a deployed process holding a dev key for each role, and a non-deployed production-image process that must still start.

## Release status

issue.title: fix(replay): keep direct block tokens on the app's own route
issue.body:
## Problem

- An export reads blocks as its creator, so a long export can rate limit that person's playback.
- The player sends its block token to any URL the listing names, built from the request's Host header.

## Changes

- A team's exports share their own viewer, `e<team id>`, so they no longer use their creator's rate limit and many exports add no budget.
- Block URLs are relative. The player sends the token only to same-origin `/replay-blocks/` URLs, else reads through Django.
- The recording-api half (dev signing keys, `nosniff`) moved to PostHog/posthog#132897, because one PR cannot mix Node with Python or frontend changes.

issue.title: feat(replay): fill player bars with blurred recording colors
issue.body:
## Problem

- Vertical mobile recordings leave most of the player as flat dark bars.

## Changes

- Bars beside a recording that does not fill the player now show a blurred extension of the recording's edge colors.
- Colors come from the replayed DOM, which cannot be redrawn blurred like video.
- Sampling runs only after the recorded page changes, so a paused or static page costs nothing.
- Background images load inside the replay frame, so the app's `img-src` policy never sees customer image URLs.
- A player menu item turns it off. Export modes and the masking overlay keep plain bars.

- Not tested: screenshot-mode native mobile recordings, and canvas-heavy recordings.

**Test rationale:** unit tests cover color parsing (Chrome's space-separated `rgb()` form), edge-aligned sampling, and edge extension.

issue.title: fix(replay): retry rate-limited direct block reads
issue.body:
## Problem

- Viewers on the direct block rollout lose playback after one rate-limited block: a single 429 from recording-api shows "We couldn't load this recording".

## Changes

- A rate-limited block now waits for `Retry-After` and retries, up to three times, while the rest of the batch keeps downloading.
- A 429 that outlasts the retries still ends playback. It never falls back to Django, which would get round the limit, even when a failing sibling block or the batch deadline cuts a wait short.
- A rate-limited batch sends one `replay direct block fetch rate limited` event.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran `snapshotDataLogic.test.ts` locally.

**Test rationale:** cases cover a 429 that recovers, one that persists, and 429s beside a failing or stalled sibling.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

- **Decisions:** the retry sits per block in `getBlocksDirectly` with `retryWithBackoff`, not around the whole batch, so blocks already downloaded are not requested again.
- **CI report:** the complexity warnings name `handleFetch` and `listLegacy` in `api.ts`, which this PR does not touch.
- **Read closely:** `pendingRateLimits` and the `.catch` in `getBlocksDirectly` that reports a pending 429 instead of a sibling's error.

+            elif self.kind == "team":

+    def __call__(self, request: HttpRequest, obj: Model, form: forms.Form) -> Page:

+            form.add_error("confirm_team_id", f"Type {obj.pk}, the ID of this team, to delete for real.")
+        dry_run = form.cleaned_data["dry_run"]
+        notice = (
+            "Dry run: nothing is deleted. The run counts the recordings that match, and its certificate says it was a dry run."
+            if dry_run
+            else f"This permanently deletes the recordings below from {obj.name} ({obj.pk}). It cannot be undone."
+        )
+        rows = [
+            Row(cells=(Cell(text="Team"), Cell(text=f"{obj.name} ({obj.pk})"))),
+            *self._scope_rows(obj, form),
+            Row(
+                cells=(
+                    Cell(text="Dry run"),
+                    Cell(text="Yes" if dry_run else "No", tone=None if dry_run else Tone.DESTRUCTIVE),
+                )
+            ),
+            Row(cells=(Cell(text="Reason"), Cell(text=form.cleaned_data["reason"]))),
+        ]
+        return Page(blocks=(Notice(text=notice), Table(columns=("What", "Value"), rows=tuple(rows))))
+
+    def _scope_rows(self, team: Team, form: forms.Form) -> list[Row]:
+        if self.kind == "person":
+            distinct_ids: list[str] = form.cleaned_data["distinct_ids"]
+            return [
+                Row(cells=(Cell(text="Recordings of"), Cell(text=f"{len(distinct_ids):,} distinct IDs"))),
+                Row(cells=(Cell(text="Distinct IDs"), Cell(text=_sample(distinct_ids), mono=True))),
+            ]
+        if self.kind == "team":
+            return [Row(cells=(Cell(text="Recordings"), Cell(text="Every recording of this team", tone=Tone.WARNING)))]
+        if self.kind == "filters":
+            assert isinstance(form, FilterDeletionForm)
+            return [Row(cells=(Cell(text="Recordings matching"), Cell(text=describe_query(form.filters().query()))))]
+        session_ids: list[str] = form.cleaned_data["csv_file"]
+        return [
+            Row(cells=(Cell(text="File"), Cell(text=form.cleaned_data["source_filename"]))),
+            Row(cells=(Cell(text="Session IDs"), Cell(text=f"{len(session_ids):,}"))),
+            Row(cells=(Cell(text="First session IDs"), Cell(text=_sample(session_ids), mono=True))),
+        ]
+
+
+def _sample(values: list[str]) -> str:
+    shown = ", ".join(values[:PREVIEW_SAMPLE_SIZE])
+    hidden = len(values) - PREVIEW_SAMPLE_SIZE

issue.title: feat(replay): cache direct replay blocks for 4 hours
issue.body:
## Problem

- A viewer's browser keeps a decrypted replay block for 24 hours, so a deleted recording stays readable from that browser's cache for a day.
- The Django snapshot route caches for 1 hour, so direct serving widens that exposure before its prod rollout.

## Changes

- Direct block responses now send `private, max-age=14400, immutable`, so the cache holds a block for 4 hours.
- Within 4 hours, seeks and re-views still read from the cache. Later views fetch each block again from recording-api.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran the recording-api Jest suite locally.

**Test rationale:** the two existing header assertions in `recording-api.test.ts` now expect the 4-hour value, and fail if the constant drifts.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

issue.title: fix(replay): log an activity row when a single recording is deleted
issue.body:
## Problem

- A user who deletes one recording, in the app or through the MCP `session-recording-delete` tool, gets no entry in the activity log.
- The Signals activity summary reads only activity log rows. So this MCP write and its agent intent never reach the user's summary.
- Bulk delete already writes a `Replay` row. Only single delete does not.

Refs #126685

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a18f51-7509-7a5e-ae24-88e77593a5fc -->
## Origin

- Issues: [#126685](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/126685)
- First signal: 2026-10-31
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a18f51-7509-7a5e-ae24-88e77593a5fc?link_source=github_pr)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P2 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a18f51-7509-7a5e-ae24-88e77593a5fc -->

## Changes

- Single recording delete now writes a `Replay` / `deleted` activity row. The row has the user, the session id and the MCP agent intent, if the request has one.
- The Activity panel shows "deleted" for it through the default describer.
- This PR does not do the gap analysis in #126685 (exec targets, failed calls, scout writes, team id mapping). That stays open in the issue.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran `test_delete_session_recording` and the bulk delete tests in `posthog/session_recordings/test/test_session_recordings.py`. They pass.
- Removed the fix and ran the test again. It failed with `ActivityLog.DoesNotExist`.

**Test rationale:** Extends `test_delete_session_recording` (app and MCP cases). It catches the regression where `destroy` writes no activity row. No other test checks the single delete audit row.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/adding-activity-logging`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

<details>

Thanks for digging into #91388, the diagnosis is spot on: mobile recordings land under the default `active_seconds > 5` filter.

We'd rather not fix it in ingestion though. `active_seconds` is meant to measure user input, and full snapshots also fire on page loads, background tabs, spinners and video, so this would raise active time for web recordings too and shift everything that filters on it. The player counts snapshots as active for a different reason (deciding what to skip during playback), which is why the two segmenters differ.

The root cause is on the SDK side: iOS and Android only send `TouchStart`/`TouchEnd`, nothing while a finger is moving, so scrolls and swipes barely register. Sending throttled `TouchMove` events during gestures would fix that without any server change, since ingestion already counts them as active. @PostHog/team-client-libraries, would you be up for picking that up?

Separately, the replay list should tell people when the activity filter is hiding recordings instead of just showing an empty list. If you'd like to take that on, it would be a great contribution. Otherwise we'll close this and track both in the issue.

issue.title: fix(replay): stop mobile screenshot replays flashing white in Safari
issue.body:
## Problem

Anyone watching a mobile screenshot replay (Flutter, iOS, Android) in Safari sees the player flash white on almost every frame, so the replay reads as flicker rather than a recording. Chrome and exported videos look fine.

Closes #107201

Each mobile screenshot arrives as a full snapshot, so the player rebuilds the iframe document for every frame. Chrome decodes the new image within the same paint. WebKit paints the iframe's white background (`.PlayerFrame__content iframe { background-color: white }`) before the image is ready, so every rebuild shows as a white frame.

## Changes

- **Safari users now see mobile replays without the per-frame flash.** When a screenshot follows another from the same window and image node, `processAllSnapshots` emits an attribute mutation that swaps the `img` `src` instead of a new full snapshot. The first frame of each source, any change of node id, and anything that isn't a single screenshot still produce a full snapshot, as today.
- Mechanical: `segmenter.ts` counts a mutation carrying `data-posthog-screenshot` as activity, so mobile recordings without touch events still aren't fast-forwarded as inactive. Web mutations never carry that attribute, and malformed mutations can't throw.

Before and after in WebKit, the same 40-screenshot recording played side by side:

![Before (left) and after (right) in WebKit](https://github.com/Lukas-io/posthog/raw/pr-assets/before-after-webkit.gif)

Twelve consecutive WebKit frames, before:

![Before: two of twelve frames are white](https://github.com/Lukas-io/posthog/raw/pr-assets/strip-before-webkit.png)

After:

![After: no white frames](https://github.com/Lukas-io/posthog/raw/pr-assets/strip-after-webkit.png)

## How did you test this code?

I used an agent (Claude Code) for this work. I didn't run it inside a PostHog dev instance or in desktop Safari by hand. What was run:

- The existing `common/replay-shared` and frontend session-recordings Jest suites, plus the new tests.
- A Playwright harness that feeds 40 Flutter-style 780×1688 screenshots through `parseJsonSnapshots` → `processAllSnapshots` → the rrweb `Replayer` with `COMMON_REPLAYER_CONFIG`, in a page styled like the player frame. It records playback at 25 fps and counts white frames. WebKit 26.4 went from 26 white flashes to 1 (the initial keyframe). Chrome 148 had 0 before and after.

**Test rationale:**
- **`process-all-snapshots.test.ts`:** consecutive same-window screenshots become one full snapshot followed by `src` mutations. A changed node id, a new source, wireframe-mode mobile and web recordings keep today's output. Android screenshot-only updates convert, and anything else keeps the synthetic full snapshot. The closest existing coverage is the mobile full-snapshot tests in this file, which only assert full snapshots, so they wouldn't catch a conversion that drops adds.
- **`segmenter.test.ts`:** a screenshot mutation counts as activity, and a web mutation without the attribute does not. Without this test, a mobile recording with no touch events would be skipped as inactive after 5 s, and none of the existing segmenter tests use mobile events.

Trade-offs for review:
1. **One flash per source, not zero.** Conversion restarts at each `blob_v2` source, so a long recording still flashes about once per source in Safari instead of every frame. Continuing across sources would need cross-source processing state, so I've left it as a possible follow-up.
2. **Seeking in WebKit** replays the mutations since the source's keyframe. Setting a ~350 KB data-URL `src` costs about 0.65 ms per frame in WebKit, a few tens of ms for a typical ≤10 s source. A periodic keyframe would cap it at one flash per keyframe; happy to add one if you prefer.
3. **Android keyboard placeholders** added by keyboard custom events now persist until the next real full snapshot, instead of being dropped by the synthetic full snapshot on each update.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

issue.body:
## Problem

- Right after a recording is deleted, its block listing still lists every block.
- The listing reads only ClickHouse, which learns of deletions later through Kafka. The key store knows at once.
- Once browsers cache blocks (#128111), the listing is the only place the player learns of a deletion.

- A listing with blocks checks the session key and returns the block route's `410 recording_deleted`.
- An empty listing skips the check: an early lookup would cache "no key" for a day and break decryption.

- After a delete, the Redis cache holds a deleted marker. Lookups only fill an empty entry, and new keys replace anything but the marker (atomic Lua). A lookup or key generation racing the delete cannot re-cache the live key.

**Test rationale:** route tests catch a shredded key listing blocks, an empty listing reading the key store, and a key store error or stall failing the listing. Key store tests run a lookup and a key generation that finish after a delete; the Lua script was also checked against a real Redis 7.

+description: >
+  Explains why part of one session recording was not captured, by reading the
+  exported rrweb JSON (`*-ph-recording.json`) and the SDK lifecycle and config

+---
+
+# Diagnosing gaps in what a replay captured
+
+The user has one recording open and something is missing: the start, the end, a page, a stretch in the middle, or other sessions that should have been recorded.
+The recording itself is the best evidence.
+posthog-js writes its config, its start reason, and its lifecycle (pauses, idle, session changes, page loads) into the recording as custom events.
+
+Your job is to separate three things:
+
+1. **Expected gaps**: the SDK did what it was configured to do (sampling, triggers, URL blocklist, idle, hidden tab, minimum duration).
+2. **Lost data**: the SDK recorded, but data did not reach PostHog (tab closed before upload, blocked `/s/` requests, a proxy that breaks `/s/`, billing limits).
+3. **Not recorded at all**: the SDK never ran or never started on those pages (a second app with replay off, recorder script blocked, init removed).
+
+Name which one it is, and back it with timestamps from this recording.
+
+## Inputs
+
+| Input                                        | What it holds                                                                                              |
+| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Attached file ending in `-ph-recording.json` | The full export, with every custom event and snapshot. Query it with `jq`. Never print it whole.           |
+| `session_recording_data` context item        | A compact timeline: page loads, console, network, custom events. Use it when no file is attached.          |
+| `posthog:execute-sql`                        | The session's events and SDK diagnostic properties. Shows pages the user visited that the recording lacks. |
+| `posthog:session-recording-get`              | Metadata: start and end time, duration, active seconds, `snapshot_source`.                                 |
+
+## Workflow
+
+### Step 1: Build the lifecycle timeline
+
+Run the recipes in [reading-the-export.md](./references/reading-the-export.md):
+
+- **Timeline**: page loads (Meta), full snapshots, and SDK custom events, in seconds from the start, with window ids.
+- **Windows**: for each `windowId`, the first event, the first full snapshot, and the last event.
+- **Gaps**: stretches of 30 seconds or more with no data.
+- **Config**: `$remote_config_received`, `$recording_started`, `triggerGroupSamplingDecisionMade`, and the replay-related keys of `$posthog_config`.
+
+Mobile SDKs do not write these custom events. For mobile, use the windows and gaps recipes and the SQL in Step 3.
+
+### Step 2: Explain each gap from the timeline
+
+Read the custom events around each gap. The [lifecycle tags table](./references/reading-the-export.md#lifecycle-custom-events) says what each one means.
+
+- `sessionIdle` before a gap and `sessionNoLongerIdle` after it: the user was inactive. Expected. The SDK takes no snapshots while idle.
+- `window hidden` / `window visible`: the user was in another tab or app. Expected.
+- `recording paused` with `reason: url blocker`: the page matched the URL blocklist. Expected.
+- `browser offline`: data was buffered offline and may be lost if the tab closed.
+- `$session_id_change` or `$session_ending`: the rest is in another recording. `nextSessionId` names it.

+
+Each cause lists its symptom, the evidence that proves it, and the fix.
+They are grouped by the three verdicts in the skill, and ordered by how often they reach support.
+Recipes are in [reading-the-export.md](./reading-the-export.md).
+

+
+### Recording conditions leave sessions or pages out
+
+**Symptom:** "only some users", "only landing pages", "nothing on mobile since the upgrade", "the subdomain stopped recording".
+
+**Evidence:**
+
+- `$remote_config_received`: `version`, `triggerGroups`, and the legacy `sampleRate`, `urlTriggers`, `eventTriggers`, `linkedFlag`, `triggerMatchType`. Read the config notes in [reading-the-export.md](./reading-the-export.md#config-fields-in-remote_config_received) to tell which of these the SDK used.
+- `$recording_started.reason` tells which condition started this recording. With legacy conditions, `sampled` only records the sampling decision. The SDK writes it before it checks triggers, so look for a later `url_trigger_matched`, `event_trigger_matched`, or `linked_flag_matched`, and read `triggerMatchType`, before you conclude a trigger never fired.
+- `triggerGroupSamplingDecisionMade` shows each group's sample rate and decision.
+- Events: `$sdk_debug_replay_url_trigger_status`, `$sdk_debug_replay_event_trigger_status`, `$sdk_debug_replay_linked_flag_trigger_status` stay `trigger_pending` on sessions that do not record.
+
+**Common mistakes:**
+
+- A URL trigger regex that cannot match. Check it against the `$current_url` values of real events, including the scheme, subdomain, and slashes.
+- An event trigger that only fires on web. Recording conditions are project-wide and shared by web and mobile, so mobile never records. Add an event that fires on mobile (for example `$screen` or `Application Opened`); event triggers combine with OR.
+- A sample rate left in the collapsed **legacy recording conditions** section of replay settings. It is a fallback: it applies when the project has no readable trigger groups, or when the SDK is too old for trigger groups (no `triggerGroupSamplingDecisionMade` events, and an old `$lib_version`). A current SDK with trigger groups ignores it. When it does apply, which pages are missing looks meaningful but is random per session.
+- The customer's own rollout flag or sampling stacked on top of PostHog sampling.
+- Mobile SDK upgrades: older Android SDKs ignored remote sampling and triggers and recorded everything. After an upgrade, the same project settings record fewer sessions.
+- A local `session_recording.sampleRate` in `posthog.init`, or `sessionReplayConfig.sampleRate` in a mobile SDK, overrides the project rate. The `sampleRate` in `$remote_config_received` is already the local rate when one is set.
+

+On web, the SDK buffers about a minute before a trigger fires, so the recording starts shortly before the trigger. Mobile SDKs have no pre-trigger buffer: recording starts at the trigger.
+Docs: https://posthog.com/docs/session-replay/how-to-control-which-sessions-you-record
+
+### Minimum duration drops short sessions
+
+**Symptom:** short visits never have a recording, or "only long sessions are recorded".
+
+**Evidence:** `minimumDurationMilliseconds` in `$remote_config_received`. Sessions shorter than it are not kept.
+
+**Fix:** lower it in recording conditions if short sessions matter.
+
+### URL blocklist pauses recording
+
+**Symptom:** a page is missing from the middle of a recording.
+
+**Evidence:** `recording paused` with `reason: url blocker`, then `recording resumed`. `urlBlocklist` in the config holds the pattern.
+
+**Fix:** none if intended. Otherwise narrow the pattern.
+
+### Idle time and hidden tabs
+
+**Symptom:** "large gaps", "the recording skips minutes", "the replay is shorter than the visit".
+
+**Evidence:** `sessionIdle` before the gap and `sessionNoLongerIdle` after it, or `window hidden` and `window visible`. The gaps recipe lines up with these.
+
+**Fix:** none. This is expected. The player skips inactivity by default.
+
+### The session rotated into another recording
+
+**Symptom:** a visit is split in two, or the end of what the user did is not in this recording.
+

issue.body:
## Problem

- A browser agent or a script can fetch snapshot blobs through a logged-in web session with no limit.
- The snapshot rate limits apply only to personal API keys.

## Changes

- Browser sessions and OAuth tokens get a per-user quota on blob fetches: 200 a minute, 3000 an hour. API keys, exports and share links keep their own limits.
- It starts log-only: over-limit fetches are served, counted as `snapshots_user_*_log_only`, and logged.
- `SNAPSHOT_USER_RATE_LIMIT_ENFORCED=true` turns on the `429`.
- Only blob fetches count. Listing a recording's sources does not.
- On a `429`, the player stops retrying and shows "You've loaded a lot of recording data in a short time. Wait a few minutes, then retry."
- `Replay/Tabs/Home/Failure/SnapshotsRateLimited` renders this overlay. It is a new surface, so there is no before.

![Player overlay after a 429 on the snapshot fetch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/e05710030b8443642c5b34014db678b476f2f3db/2026/11/f3a8cb13-c9ad-4213-b20e-89cd15130355.png)

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** a blob_v2 API test fails if enforcement misses or log-only blocks. A `snapshotDataLogic` case fails if a `429` retries.

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5)

**Skills:** `/improving-drf-endpoints`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/working-with-storybook`, `/stacking-prs`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** 3000/hour, not 1500, because normal viewing of long recordings reaches about 2000 fetches an hour.
- **Decisions:** the view checks the quota by hand, not through `throttle_classes`, so only blob fetches count.
- **Follow-ups:** after a week of log-only data, set the enforced limit and flip `SNAPSHOT_USER_RATE_LIMIT_ENFORCED`.
- **Read closely:** the quota check before `_stream_blob_v2_to_client` in `snapshots`, and the `Throttled` re-raise.

</details>
